clue.text: Country lady crossed road

indicators.note: the lady's name is crossed by the road, which runs through the middle of it

parts.note: Joan is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman makes her way across a road somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a rural adjective but it is the definition, a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jordan is a Middle Eastern kingdom, a nation state.

clue.text: Bill getting work outside from another man

indicators.note: the word for work is placed around the outside of the word for bill

parts.note: a job is a piece of work
AC (account) is a bill, as in a tradesman's account

explanation.surface: Someone gets a bill for a job done outside, sent by some other fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: AC, short for account, is a common crossword stand-in for a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob is a male first name, so a further man.

clue.text: Management course

definitions.meaning: the running or guiding of an enterprise
the line or route something takes

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: control of an organisation, and the path or heading something follows.

clue.text: Ninety-nine vehemently entered ancient city

indicators.note: the city has entered the run of letters across these two words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone announces with great force that ninety-nine people went into an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the second 'nine' of Ninety-nine and finishes three letters into vehemently.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineveh was the capital of the Assyrian empire, a city of antiquity on the Tigris.

clue.text: Georgia has flimsy lamp

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
's is the contraction of has, as in he's got
light, as in light fabric, means thin and flimsy

explanation.surface: A Georgian household owns a feeble lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' supplies only an S, as the contraction 's.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaslight is a lamp burning coal gas, as in old street lighting.

clue.text: Not a particular occasion for voting?

definitions.text: Not a particular occasion for voting?

parts.words: Not a particular occasion for voting?
parts.note: read 'not particular' as general in the broad sense, and the occasion for voting as a poll; together a nationwide poll

explanation.definitionFit: A national poll to choose a whole parliament, as against a by-election for one seat.

clue.text: City bird on the water

parts.note: a swan is a large waterbird
the sea is the water, as in going over the water

explanation.surface: A bird is floating out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the bird above the water. Swansea is a city in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in Wales, a large urban settlement.

clue.text: Charm of cricketing county shortly belongs to us

parts.note: GLAM is the short form of Glamorgan, the Welsh first-class county cricket team
something that belongs to us is ours

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that a county cricket side's charisma is their own.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan is a historic county of Wales whose cricket club plays in the English County Championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring attractiveness, much like charm or allure.

clue.text: Getting goal whilst preparing to shoot!

parts.note: taking means getting or obtaining
an aim is a goal or objective

explanation.surface: A footballer gets a goal at the very moment of lining up a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' and 'shoot' suggest football, but the definition is a marksman sighting a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lining up a gun or bow on a target before firing.

clue.text: Many an article by Ronnie on fruit

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
it can mean a thing or an object, an article
Ron is the short form of Ronnie

explanation.surface: A great many items are placed by Ronnie on top of some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' tempts as a grammatical article (A, THE); here it is an object, IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A citron is a large thick-skinned citrus fruit like a lemon.

clue.text: No exclamation of surprise on island boat

parts.note: taken as written
ah is a cry of surprise
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Someone is unsurprised, perhaps, to find no boat on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is a small island in the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's Ark is the vessel of the Genesis Flood story.

clue.text: Blanket insurance debutante shortly arranged first

indicators.note: the rearranged short word is placed first, in front of the insurance word
the short form of debutante is arranged into a new order

parts.note: deb is the short form of debutante
cover is insurance protection

explanation.surface: A debutante's insurance policy is sorted out in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blanket' reads like an adjective qualifying insurance, as in blanket cover, but it is the definition; 'first' tells you the shuffled short word leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedcover is a spread laid over a bed, a coverlet.

clue.text: Volatile lady has nothing on in lounge

parts.note: Sal is a woman's name, and sal volatile is smelling salts
O is a zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A temperamental woman lounges about wearing no clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sal volatile is smelling salts, so 'Volatile' playfully tags the lady as Sal.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a lounge bar or a public room for gathering.

clue.text: Top tin hazel removed

indicators.note: the letters are moved around from their positions, re-moved

explanation.surface: Tin is taken off the top of a hazel tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved, letters moved again into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Zenithal is an adjective meaning at the highest point overhead, as top can be.

clue.text: Nothing assessed, not subject to tax

parts.note: zero is nothing
rated means valued or assessed

explanation.surface: An item valued at nothing escapes any taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero-rated goods carry VAT at a nil rate, so effectively untaxed.

clue.text: Marinade I'm mixing with this lady

indicators.note: the letters of marinade are mixed, and once mixed contain the woman's name plus the letters of I'm

explanation.surface: A cook stirs up a marinade with a female friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and M out of MARINADE and rearrange the rest; 'mixing' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea is a woman's first name, so a lady.

clue.text: Utterly depressed on one side only

parts.note: down means low in spirits
right is one of the two sides, as against left

explanation.surface: Someone feels thoroughly gloomy, but only on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means thoroughly or completely, as an adverb like utterly.

clue.text: Rod held by soldiers in the country

indicators.note: the rod word is held inside the soldiers word

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, gunners of the British Army
a wand is a slender rod

explanation.surface: Troops keep a rod in their possession while deployed abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a common crossword stand-in for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a nation of central Africa.

clue.text: Ten play around when it is in full supply

indicators.note: the letters of ten play are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Ten people mess around at play while everything is in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplenty means in abundance, plentifully available.

clue.text: Authorise a very quiet walkabout?

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
a rove is a ramble or wander, a walkabout

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to sanction a silent stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve is to sanction or give official consent.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic doctor fighting leading militants

parts.note: St Luke is described as a physician in the New Testament
war is fighting

indicators.note: the leading letter of militants is taken

explanation.surface: A half-hearted medic goes into battle at the head of some militants.
explanation.walkthrough: Luke the evangelist is 'the beloved physician', hence doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means tepid, figuratively half-hearted.

clue.text: Galley where Kenneth can contain his restless desire

indicators.note: the short name can hold the desire word inside it

parts.note: Ken is the short form of Kenneth
an itch is a restless desire or urge

explanation.surface: In a ship's galley a man keeps his wanderlust in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galley' suggests a ship, but it is just the cooking room aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the cookroom on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Arrive with more expensive bread

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
prices that are up are higher

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to find the bread has gone up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: Roll up is informal for turn up, to come or get somewhere.

clue.text: Drop of water in sight?

definitions.meaning: a large waterfall, a steep drop of a river
a clouding of the lens of the eye, affecting vision

explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall plunging downward, and an eye condition dimming vision.

clue.text: Easily annoyed if left to give evidence

indicators.note: if is left out, taken away from the evidence word

parts.note: to testify is to give evidence in court
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness gets irritable when told to take the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as going away: IF departs from TESTIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable and short-tempered.

clue.text: Cooking at indoor extravaganza

indicators.note: an extravaganza is a wild, elaborate show, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Food is being prepared at a big indoor festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is a style of Indian cookery in a clay oven.

clue.text: Soldier among old women with meat dish

indicators.note: the soldier word sits among the letters of the old women word

parts.note: hags are ugly old women
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A serviceman dines with some elderly ladies on a meaty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggis is the Scottish dish of sheep's offal and oats cooked in a stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a Scottish savoury pudding of minced offal.

clue.text: Dyer can travel round lake and remove dirt

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the lake letter
the letters of dyer can travel about into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A cloth dyer can go round a lake and wash things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travel' makes DRYCEAN of Dyer can, and 'round' wraps it about L.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry-clean is to wash fabric with solvents rather than water.

clue.text: Not a railway official

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are not a railway employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a legal officer who certifies documents.
